notes: THE RIGS a contact may shove. A species named here has its SKELETON baked into fish.mesh (joints, weights, the parent of each bone and its rest transform) instead of being flattened onto one identity bone; a species with no row bakes exactly as it always did and reacts through the vertex dent alone. One row per chain, root first, tip last. `bones` is the chain's bone names separated by |, copied VERBATIM from the springChains of path/src/assets.js — the same rigs, already measured and tuned against these same .glb files. The names there are the ones GLTFLoader produced, which have had their DOTS STRIPPED: the raw node in greatwhite.glb is `Bone.003_Armature_5`. The baker matches on the stripped spelling so either form resolves, and it FAILS on a name that misses rather than dropping the chain, because a silently dropped chain is how the orca cow lost her whole dorsal on half of all boss arrivals. `role` is what the chain is for and what its looseness is keyed on: a `tail` is the body's own run of spine, a `fin` is a control surface that should lag rather than stream
the orca's two flippers are BOTH called L in the rig; Shoulder_L1 is the right one. Copied as it is rather than corrected, because the name is the model's
the two orcas were cut from one family file and share a rig, so they share their chains
